# Axial Skyrmions
- The reflection used here flips the sign of only one pion field, so the relative phase definition differs by π from that of refs.[3, 12, 7], where the antiSkyrmion is formed by reversing all three pion fields.
- This convention is adopted because it allows a more natural analogy with the corresponding case of monopoles.
- The profile function vanishes at a distance s/2 from the centre of the Skyrmion (or antiSkyrmion), allowing the Skyrmion and antiSkyrmion to be smoothly joined, with fields set to the vacuum outside their cores (3.10).
- Besides the simple ansatz (3.7), more refined initial conditions were constructed from the rational map ansatz [11] employing an axially symmetric charge n map.
